commit_message:
Sprint review: fix #123 (symlink + '..' escape, scoped len/bool), tests first (#127)

* test: cover the #107/#119 surface; strict-xfail repros of #123

Adds tests on the unchanged code for the sprint's containment and scoping
changes: path_is_under on mixed absolute/relative paths, the zip readers'
in-root read/write paths, the deprecated MakeMissingDirsStoreMixin refusing
out-of-root keys, Store.head's fallback, and len/bool of unscoped stores.

The two #123 defects (symlink + '..' escaping rootdir; len/bool counting
out-of-scope ids) are pinned as strict xfails, flipped by the fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: a '..' after a symlink no longer escapes rootdir (#123)

path_is_under is lexical, so root/lnk/../x passed it while the OS resolved
it to the parent of lnk's target. FileSysCollection.is_in_root now also
requires dotdot_resolves_lexically(k): the part of the key up to its last
'..' must resolve the same way physically (realpath) and lexically. Keys
without a '..' segment take a string-only fast path, so listing and the
design #107 kept (a symlinked sub-directory of the root is addressable) are
unchanged. Every containment user (Files*, DirReader, PickleStores, the zip
readers, mk_dirs_if_missing) goes through is_in_root, so all are covered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: len and bool of a scoped store agree with its iteration (#123)

Since #119, iterating a prefix/suffix-scoped store skips out-of-scope ids,
but Store.__len__ still returned len(self.store): KeyCodecs.prefixed('p/')
over {'stray': 0} iterated nothing yet had len 1 and was truthy.

A key mapping that can raise OutOfScopeKeyError is now marked with
dol.errors.raises_out_of_scope. Store.__len__ counts in-scope ids for a
marked layer (a scan) and keeps the inner len otherwise, so unscoped
layers over DB-backed stores keep their cheap count; Store.__bool__ stops
at the first in-scope id. The mark is set on the affix decoder (when it
has a prefix or suffix), PrefixRelativizationMixin and
RelativePathKeyMapper, and carried by wrap_kvs (_wrap_outcoming, including
to subclasses of a scoped class) and by Pipe (so composed codecs keep it).

Also: one _strip_prefix helper for the two prefix mappers in paths.py,
the dead _prefix_length cache removed (it went stale on prefix
reassignment, which is why #115 stopped using it), and the doubled 'so'
in the out-of-scope error messages.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: one pickle-security warning in dol.misc, pointed to from each class

#117 pasted the same five-line Security note into five docstrings, with
URL advice that only applies to get_obj. The module docstring holds the
full warning; each docstring now points to it in two lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: review findings on the #123 fixes

- A rootdir holding a '..' after a symlink (join(dirname(__file__), '..',
  'data') in a symlink-installed package) made every key fail the new
  check, so the store looked empty. dotdot_resolves_lexically now takes a
  keyword-only base: is_in_root passes rootdir, whose own '..' is resolved
  as the OS does, and only the key's part beyond it is checked.
- Store.__len__ asks the inner len first, so an inner store that refuses
  len (to spare list() a second listing, as s3dol does) still refuses it,
  and an empty inner store costs no scan.
- The scope mark survives FirstArgIsMapping; may_raise_out_of_scope
  returns a real bool; the docs say a hand-overridden _key_of_id must be
  marked itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: Windows semantics for the symlink and zip tests

Windows normalizes '..' lexically before following links, so 'lnk/../x'
is 'root/x' there: nothing escapes, and the tests now assert containment
instead of refusal on Windows. ZipFilesReader's default subpath is
POSIX-only (as the #111 test already notes), so its test skips there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
